item.title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78649-9

Water structures govern the behaviour of solutes across aqueous bulk and interfacial environments. Here the authors use weakly hydrated anions to reshape hydration in the bulk and at interfaces, thereby regulating amine monomer partitioning and interfacial transport while suppressing acyl chloride hydrolysis during polyamide-forming interfacial polymerization.
item.dc:title: Breaking water-structure constraints by Hofmeister effects in interfacial polymerization for polyamide membranes

item.title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78604-8

Structural isomers can be difficult to distinguish and map by mass alone. This study shows that Orbitrap-SIMS can separate and image isomeric sugars directly on surfaces, offering a new route to study complex biomolecules.
item.dc:title: Spatially resolving isomeric trisaccharides on surfaces with Orbitrap-SIMS

item.title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78524-7

Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) typically require chiral precursors or catalysts to achieve asymmetry. Here, the authors report the enantioselective synthesis of chemically chiral COFs using circularly polarized light as the sole chiral director.
item.dc:title: Optical-handedness-driven enantioselective synthesis and programmable chirality encoding of covalent organic frameworks

item.title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78906-x

Brassinosteroids are widely used in agriculture, but their modes of action remain incompletely understood. Here, the authors show that brassinosteroids inhibit BIN2, leading to KIN10 degradation and activation of gene expression and nitrogen assimilation enzymes.
item.dc:title: Brassinosteroids improve nitrogen utilization by antagonizing BIN2-mediated SnRK1 activation

item.title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78873-3

Turning waste plastic into valuable chemicals requires precise control of competing reactions. This study shows that tuning ruthenium particle size enables selective conversion of polyethylene terephthalate into p-xylylenediamine.
item.dc:title: Size-dependent catalysis of Ru nanoparticles for selective reductive amination of PET plastic

item.title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78949-0

Here, the authors show that the cell-surface protein ADAM17 blocks HIV-1 by preventing maturation of the viral envelope protein, while the viral protein Nef counteracts this effect by redirecting ADAM17 out of infected cells.
item.dc:title: ADAM17 is a broad HIV-1 restriction factor targeted by Nef to restore Env maturation

item.title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78765-6

Diabetes impairs wound healing by disrupting macrophage metabolism and angiogenesis. Here, authors identify macrophage-specific transketolase (TKT) as a metabolic checkpoint and develop a nanozyme hydrogel that restores macrophage TKT to promote vascular repair in diabetic wounds.
item.dc:title: Metabolic reprogramming of macrophage-specific transketolase orchestrates angiogenesis in diabetic wounds

item.title: Nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage lithium batteries via preemptive passivation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 17 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78701-8

Batteries require safe electrolytes without compromising performance. Here, the authors develop a nonflammable sulfamoyl–carbonate hybrid electrolyte for high-voltage, long-lasting, and safe lithium-ion batteries.

item.title: Multifunctional submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78691-7

Ultrasound carbonation confines water distribution, creating submicron-scale porous water-foamed cementitious materials that combine low density, high specific strength, improved sound insulation and CO2 uptake without conventional foaming agents.

item.title: Intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in Healthy Volunteers with Artificially-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuresis - a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78333-y

Apelin can counteract water retention and may help correct low blood sodium. Here, the authors show in a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial that intravenous apelin does not meaningfully increase urine output in adults with experimentally induced hyponatremia.
item.dc:title: Intravenous [Pyr¹]apelin-13 in Healthy Volunteers with Artificially-Induced Syndrome of Inappropriate Antidiuresis - a double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover study

item.title: Early warnings of earthquakes
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76605-1

Earthquakes are among the most destructive natural hazards. As populations in seismically active regions grow, the need for effective risk mitigation strategies is more urgent than ever. In that regard, earthquake early warning systems are a key component to reduce the impact of seismic shaking.
item.dc:title: Early warnings of earthquakes

item.title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78569-8

Regulatory genetic variants can influence disease risk through effects on chromatin activity, but studying these effects across tissues remains challenging. Here, the authors use cell‑free chromatin profiling to identify chromatin quantitative trait loci across diverse tissues, linking regulatory variation to hundreds of human traits and diseases.
item.dc:title: Circulating chromatin reveals effects of disease-associated variants on gene regulation

item.title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 16 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78619-1

Continuous glucose monitoring is central to diabetes management, yet conventional testing provides only intermittent snapshots and may miss clinically important glycaemic fluctuations. Here, the authors present a wrist-worn hollow microneedle platform that combines active interstitial fluid extraction with nonenzymatic electrochemical glucose sensing in a wearable format. Its detachable microneedle cartridge enables independent cleaning or replacement, supporting quasi-continuous monitoring while improving practicality and long-term usability for wearable glucose tracking.
item.dc:title: Regenerable, closed-loop, nonenzymatic continuous glucose monitoring enabled by in situ electrochemical interfacial alkalinization
